extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, policymakers, funders, and potential partners interested in environmental decision science
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional 'About' page describing the Center for Research on Environmental Decisions (CRED): its mission, history, objectives, activities, and partnerships. Intended to inform readers about the center's focus and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study decision making under climate uncertainty and environmental risk
rubrics_metrics.description: CRED is an interdisciplinary center that studies individual and group decision making under climate uncertainty and decision making in the face of environmental risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes understanding both individual and group behaviors when faced with uncertain climate information and environmental hazards; research spans laboratory and field settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve communication and increase use of scientific information on climate variability and change
rubrics_metrics.description: CRED’s objectives address improved communication and increased use of scientific information on climate variability and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work aims to make scientific findings more usable for decision makers and the public, including through communication guides and advising organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance fundamental theory in social science disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to applied work, CRED advances fundamental theory in psychology, behavioral economics, and other social science disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research contributes to theoretical understanding that underpins applied interventions; the center balances theory-building with application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct integrated field projects applying decision science to sustainable development challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: CRED researchers work on integrated field projects around the world, bringing decision science to bear on sustainable development challenges (e.g., agricultural decisions and water management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field projects are used to test theories in real-world contexts and to develop contextually appropriate interventions and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidirectional flow between research and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: The flow between research and outreach goes in both directions: research informs outreach and outreach provides research opportunities to test hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach activities (education, communication guides, advising, decision support tools) both apply research findings and generate new research questions and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop decision support tools and outreach to facilitate use of scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: CRED carries out outreach including education, communication guides, advising to organizations, and the development of decision support tools which facilitate use of scientific information and promote better group decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools and outreach are evaluated by their ability to increase use of scientific information and improve collective decision outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize group decision processes in addition to individual action
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRED proposal emphasized the importance of group decisions, as well as individual actions in a group context, for climate-related and other environmental decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research priorities include studying how individual decision principles extend to groups and how group context shapes selection and implementation of actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary collaboration between physical and social scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: CRED was built from collaborations between physical and social scientists to improve utilization of scientific information about climate and hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative work across disciplines is a core principle, leveraging expertise from geosciences, climate science, and social sciences to address decision problems.
